title: Want only this world, and you get paid only here.
subtitle: Deeds done for worldly gain are paid in worldly coin
then: Ibn Abbas said those who show off are {trap}given their reward in this life{/trap}, so no one is wronged even a speck. Mujahid said it is about people who do deeds to be seen. Qatadah said the believer is {reward}rewarded in this life and the next{/reward}.
now: You post the photo of the charity box, or pray a little longer when the in-laws are watching. The praise comes, and it feels good. {trap}That may be the whole payment.{/trap} The same deed done quietly for Allah gets paid twice.
old: As long as I do good, it does not matter who sees it.
new: The reason I do a good deed decides where it gets paid.
try: Do one good thing today that nobody will ever know about.

title: Deeds that looked impressive, but weighed nothing.
subtitle: What is left of work done only for the world
then: This verse finishes the thought of the previous one. Ibn Abbas said that a person who prays or fasts only for worldly benefit {trap}has his deed wasted{/trap}, since he only sought this world. Ibn Kathir adds that whoever strives for the Hereafter as a believer {reward}has his striving appreciated{/reward}.
now: You spend years building a reputation as the generous one at work. Every gift is noted, every favor remembered. {idea}Ask who it is really for.{/idea} The same hours can be turned toward Allah with one honest change of heart.
old: I have done so much good that I must be fine.
new: Good deeds only last if they were for Allah, so I keep checking why I do them.
try: Before one task today, pause and say quietly: this is for You, O Allah.

title: Your inner nature already recognizes the truth.
subtitle: Clear proof inside, a witness from outside
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer stands on {idea}the fitrah, the natural faith Allah placed in people{/idea}. Every child is born on it. The Quran then comes as a witness that matches it, and the Book of Musa came before as a guide. {trap}So be in no doubt about it.{/trap}
now: You look at a newborn in the hospital nursery and feel that something greater made this. No lecture told you that. {idea}That feeling is the first witness.{/idea} The Quran does not argue with it; it agrees with it.
old: Faith is something I have to be talked into.
new: My own nature already leans toward Allah, and the Quran confirms what it knows.
try: Spend two minutes today looking at something in nature and let your heart say who made it.

title: The worst wrong is lying about Allah.
subtitle: Two ways people stand before Him

row.title: His covering
sub: for those who turned to Him

then: Ibn Umar reported that Allah will draw the believer near, {reward}cover him from the people{/reward}, and remind him of his sins one by one. When he thinks he is ruined, Allah says: I hid these for you in the world and I forgive them today. {trap}The ones who lied about their Lord are named openly.{/trap}
now: You have messed up in ways nobody knows. Allah kept it hidden, day after day. {reward}That covering is a mercy you can lean into.{/reward} Never put words in Allah's name that He did not say, and keep asking Him to keep covering you.
old: My hidden sins mean I am already lost.
new: The One who has hidden my sins all this time can forgive them too, if I turn to Him.
try: Make a short dua today: O Allah, cover me in this world and the next.

title: Blocking the path, then calling it crooked.
subtitle: Turning others away from Allah's way
then: Ibn Kathir explains that these people {trap}kept others from the truth and the path of guidance{/trap}, and so kept them from Paradise. They wanted the path to look crooked. At the root, they did not believe in the Hereafter at all.
now: Your younger cousin starts praying and you joke that she has gone extreme. Or you make religion sound harsh when someone asks you a question. {idea}You can be the person who makes the path look easy.{/idea}
old: What I say about religion only affects me.
new: My words and jokes can push someone toward Allah or away, so I choose them with care.
try: Encourage one person today in a good thing they are trying to do.

title: Ears and eyes given, but never used for truth.
subtitle: No escape and no protector besides Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}could not escape on earth{/trap}, and had no protector besides Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah gives the oppressor respite until He seizes him. Their punishment is doubled because they were given {reward}hearing, sight and hearts{/reward} and used none of them for the truth.
now: You have ears for a podcast every commute, eyes for hours of screens a day. {idea}The same tools can turn toward what helps you.{/idea} Hearing is a gift, and so is noticing what you keep tuning out.
old: I am too busy to listen to reminders right now.
new: My hearing and sight are gifts I will be asked about, so I give some of them to the truth.
try: Swap one song or clip today for five minutes of Quran recitation.

title: They lost themselves, and their idols left them.
subtitle: What people invent besides Allah walks away
then: Ibn Kathir says what they invented, {trap}the rivals and idols besides Allah{/trap}, left them and did not help them at all. In fact those things harmed them. Those who were followed will disown those who followed them.
now: The influencer you quoted for years, the strategy you trusted, the status you chased. When the real test comes, {trap}none of it shows up for you.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you are leaning on that cannot hold you.{/idea}
old: The things I count on will always be there for me.
new: Anything I put in Allah's place will walk away from me when I need it most.
try: Name one thing you lean on more than Allah. Ask Him today to be your first support.

title: The worst trade anyone can make.
subtitle: The greatest losers, in the long run
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a {trap}transaction for the abode of the Hereafter{/trap}. They swapped the highest levels for the lowest, and {reward}nearness to Allah{/reward} for His anger. So it is no injustice that they are the greatest losers.
now: You would never trade a house for a phone case. Yet a long day can go by trading prayer time for scrolling, honesty for a small sale. {idea}Look at your trades the way a merchant does.{/idea}
old: Small choices today do not change the big picture.
new: My daily trades add up to the final account, so I want to stop trading the lasting for the cheap.
try: Notice one small trade today where you swap the better thing for the easier one, and switch it.

title: Believe, do good, and bow your heart to your Lord.
subtitle: The people of Paradise, forever
then: After describing the losers, the verse praises the believers. Ibn Kathir says {idea}their hearts believed and their limbs did good{/idea}, in words and actions. They will live in Paradise forever, {reward}and will see the Creator of the heavens and the earth{/reward}.
now: You finish your prayer and rush straight to the next notification. Or you give charity and quietly feel better than others. {idea}The verse adds a third thing: humility.{/idea} The deed lands better when the heart bows with it.
old: As long as I do the right things, my attitude does not matter.
new: Faith and good deeds are completed by a heart that humbles itself before Allah.
try: After your next prayer, stay seated one more minute and just thank Him, quietly.

title: Can the blind and the seeing ever be equal?
subtitle: The parable of the two groups
then: Ibn Kathir explains the parable. The one who rejects is {trap}blind to the truth and deaf to the proofs{/trap}. The believer {idea}sees the truth, tells it apart from falsehood, and follows the good{/idea}. Then the verse asks: will you not take heed?
now: Two coworkers hear the same rumor. One checks before sharing; the other forwards it to ten people. {idea}Same ears, different hearing.{/idea} Seeing clearly is a choice you make many times a day.
old: I see things the way they are.
new: Real sight is noticing the truth and following it, and I can ask Allah for more of it.
try: Before you share or react to anything today, stop and ask if it is true.

title: Nuh begins with the same clear warning.
subtitle: The first messenger to idol worshippers
then: The surah introduction says Allah teaches through the stories of past prophets. Ibn Kathir says Nuh was {idea}the first messenger sent to people of the earth{/idea} who worshipped idols. He warned them {trap}openly{/trap} against Allah's punishment if they kept worshipping others.
now: You hear the same advice from your grandmother, your teacher and a stranger at the mosque. It feels repetitive. {idea}Some messages repeat because they are true.{/idea} Nuh said what Hud and every prophet would say after him.
old: I have heard this reminder too many times already.
new: The message repeats across every prophet because it is the oldest truth there is.
try: Listen to one familiar reminder today as if you were hearing it for the first time.

title: Worship Allah alone, because I fear for you.
subtitle: A warning spoken out of care
then: Nuh's call was the same as the opening of this surah: {idea}worship none but Allah{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains his words as: if you keep doing this, Allah will punish you severely in the Hereafter. Nuh says {reward}I fear for you{/reward}, the voice of someone who cares.
now: You see your brother slipping into a habit that is hurting him. You can lecture him, or you can say: I am worried about you. {reward}Fear for someone is a form of love.{/reward}
new: A real warning comes from fear for the person, the way Nuh spoke to his people.
try: Tell one person you care about that you worry for them, gently and without blame.

title: They judged the message by who followed it.
subtitle: The chiefs looked down on the poor believers
then: The chiefs said Nuh was only human and {trap}only the lowest of us follow you{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says truth is not rejected because of the low status of its followers. Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan if the Prophet's ﷺ followers were noble or weak, then said {idea}the weak are the followers of the messengers{/idea}.
now: You dismiss an idea at work because the intern suggested it, then praise it when the manager repeats it. {idea}The truth does not change with the person saying it.{/idea} Check yourself before you check their rank.
old: If important people do not believe it, it is probably not true.
new: Truth is true whoever holds it, and the humble who follow it are the honored ones.
try: Listen fully today to someone you usually overlook, and take their point seriously.
